answer: To secure decentralized networks against mass identity spoofing without relying on a central authority, an agent economy can tether digital autonomy to physical infrastructure, much like verifying cargo manifests at a secure wharf rather than trusting an unvetted fable. An attacker attempting to forge thousands of AI personas faces prohibitive computational and cryptographic bounds, because each valid node requires verifiable hardware roots of trust and staked economic collateral that scale linearly with identity creation, making mass Sybil deployment economically irrational.
